newsitem.title: UK: Commonwealth chief pays tribute to Jamaica's Manley.
newsitem.headline: Commonwealth chief pays tribute to Jamaica's Manley.

text.p: Commonwealth Secretary General Emeka Anyaoku on Friday paid tribute to former Jamaican Prime Minister Michael Manley who has died aged 72, calling him "a statesman of courage and conviction."
In a letter to Jamaica's current prime minister, P.J. Patterson, Anyaoku said he had learned of Manley's death "with profound regret and sadness".
Manley was "a true believer in internationalism, he was a statesman of courage and conviction who extended his vision of a better and more just society beyond his island shores," said Anyaoku.

"Michael had the capacity for geniune friendship and fellowship that endeared him not only to his Commonwealth colleagues but to people in so many parts of the world. His passing will be deeply mourned in the Commonwealth and beyond."
Manley, prime minister of Jamaica from 1972 until 1980 and again from 1989 to 1992, died after a long battle with prostate cancer, his family said on Friday.
